newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rupiah depreciation policy unchanged - Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Rupiah depreciation policy unchanged - Indonesia.

text.p: Indonesia's policy to depreciate the rupiah remains unchanged after a rate cut on Wednesday, an official at the nation's central bank said.

C. Harinowo, director of the money market department at Bank Indonesia, also told Reuters Financial Television that Wednesday's decision to cut the discount rate for short-term securities was based on an improved outlook on inflation in Indonesia.
Harinowo, in Jakarta, was interviewed by phone from Tokyo.
Asked how Wednesday's rate cut fit in with the country's policy of guiding its currency lower, Harinowo said: "The depreciation policy will remain the same."
Harinowo said both internal and external factors had contributed to the decision to cut rates today.
The domestic factor he cited was the improved outlook for price stability.
"If interest rates remain the same, then the real interest rates will be much higher," he said.

Real rates are nominal interest rates minus inflation. Government officials have projected that inflation will fall below six percent in the current fiscal year that ends on March 31, down from more than nine percent at the start of calendar 1996.
High Indonesian interest rates relative to those in other countries gave the central bank room to ease, he said.
"There is also room on the external side to lower rates," he said.
But Harinowo said the central bank will watch the impact of today's rate cut on the market before deciding whether to ease again.
"We don't want to get complacent that we will continuously cut interest rates in the future," he said.
Bank Indonesia cut its discount rate for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points on Wednesday. SBPUs are papers purchased by the central bank to inject liquidity into the banking system.
The easing follows a 50-basis point cut in the discount rate in December.
